sections.h2: Where is Gloucester, Massachusetts, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Gloucester is a coastal city in Essex County that occupies most of the eastern end of Cape Ann, on the North Shore. It lies about 31 miles northeast of Boston, and it is far more water than most cities: of its 41.5 square miles, 15.3 are water.

The Annisquam River splits the city in half. At its southern end the river connects to Gloucester Harbor through the Blynman Canal. Only three links join the two halves: the canal bridge, the A. Piatt Andrew Memorial Bridge that carries Route 128, and the Boston and Maine railroad bridge just north of the canal.

The urban core sits on the north side of the harbor, and the rest of the city is made up of separate neighborhoods, so houses in different parts of Gloucester can feel like they belong to different towns.

  • East Gloucester, including Eastern Point and Rocky Neck
  • Downtown and the Harbor area
  • Annisquam, Bay View, Lanesville, Folly Cove and Riverdale
  • West Gloucester, including the Wingaersheek area and Magnolia

sections.h2: How old is Gloucester, and what is its history?
sections.html:
Gloucester was first settled in 1623 when men from the Dorchester Company set up a fishing outpost. That first settlement was abandoned around 1626, and the town was formally incorporated in 1642. It became a city in 1873.

Gloucester is known as America's oldest seaport. Samuel de Champlain mapped the harbor in 1606, and the Agawam people lived in the area before English settlement. The city later grew around fishing, shipbuilding and granite quarrying. Portuguese and Italian immigrants arrived in the late nineteenth century to work in the fishing industry, and their influence still shows in local festivals such as St. Peter's Fiesta, held the last weekend in June.

sections.h2: What does Gloucester's economy depend on?
sections.html:
Gloucester's economy still centers on the harbor, along with arts, tourism and marine research. In 2013 the port ranked 21st in the nation for fish landings, with 62 million pounds caught and an estimated value of $42 million.

Gorton's of Gloucester, founded in 1849, is a major seafood business based in the city, and Ocean Alliance, a marine conservation organization, is headquartered here. The Rocky Neck Art Colony is described as the oldest working art colony in the country, and the Cape Ann Museum and Gloucester Stage Company add year-round activity.

Gloucester is described as a popular summer destination, and that brings the city's short-term rental rules into play for sellers whose houses have been rented out, covered below.

Gloucester has an older population than most Massachusetts cities. The 2020 census counted 29,729 people and a median age of 50.4, and 25.3 percent of residents were 65 or older.

There are roughly 1,800 more housing units than households, a gap that can include vacant, seasonal or second homes. Owners who inherit a Gloucester house from an older relative often live elsewhere and need a sale that does not require them to come back repeatedly.

sections.h2: How does the weather affect Gloucester houses?
sections.html:
Gloucester sits between Ipswich Bay and Massachusetts Bay, and the exposure shapes both the climate and the housing. Normals show about 47 inches of precipitation and 42 inches of snow per year, with record temperatures from minus 15 to 100 degrees Fahrenheit.

Salt air, wind and coastal storms wear on roofs, siding, decks and windows. Buyers' inspectors tend to look closely at those items and at basement moisture. The city's Inspectional Services pages list a floodplain development permit application, so if your property is near the water, ask the city whether it sits in a flood zone before you describe it to a buyer.

sections.h2: How do you get to and around Gloucester?
sections.html:
Gloucester is at the northern end of Route 128, and Routes 127, 127A and 133 also run through the city. The MBTA Newburyport/Rockport Line stops in West Gloucester and Downtown Gloucester, and the Cape Ann Transportation Authority serves the city and nearby towns.

The nearest national and international flights are at Boston's Logan International Airport. The nearest local airport is Beverly Municipal Airport. Buyers who commute to Boston often pay close attention to how far a house is from either rail stop.

Gloucester Public Schools includes Gloucester High School, O'Maley Innovation Middle School, and several elementary schools: East Veterans, Plum Cove, Beeman and West Parish. The district also runs a preschool. Check with the district for the school that serves a specific address.

sections.h2: How and when does Gloucester bill property tax?
sections.html:
Gloucester bills quarterly. Bills are scheduled to be issued on July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1, and each is due 30 days after issuance. The first two are preliminary bills based on 25 percent of last year's tax. The third and fourth bills carry the actual amounts, once the assessed values and tax rate are set.

  • Abatement applications must be filed in a window that runs from the third quarter bill, typically January 1, to its due date, typically February 1. The deadline is firm.
  • A 1 percent Community Preservation Act surcharge, approved by city voters in 2008, appears on the bill.
  • Personal exemptions use a July 1 qualification date and an April 1 application deadline.

Details are on the city's assessor FAQ. Ask your closing attorney to split the quarter in progress between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What does Gloucester require before a house sale closes?
sections.html:
The Fire Prevention Bureau handles real estate transfer inspections, and appointments are scheduled through the city's ViewPoint Cloud online permitting system. Fees are collected at the time of inspection online, or by check to the inspector.

One easy-to-miss rule is house numbering. Gloucester's ordinance, Section 21-4, requires numbers at least three inches tall in a contrasting color, visible from the street. A building without the right number cannot be approved for transfer, and a revisit costs $50. The bureau also points sellers to the state's smoke and carbon monoxide requirements, which vary with the age of the home. See the city's guidance for realtors.

sections.h2: What are Gloucester's short-term rental rules?
sections.html:
Gloucester adopted a short-term rental ordinance that took effect April 1, 2025, under Section 5-63 of the city code. A short-term rental is a property rented for 30 days or less, and operators must register for a permit through the online permitting system.

Requirements include an information binder in the unit, working smoke and carbon monoxide detectors with a battery log, two egress doors, and a safe and sanitary condition throughout. If you are selling a house that has been used as a summer rental, the permit and compliance status should be part of the conversation with any buyer. The full list is on the city's short-term rental guidelines.

sections.h2: What are the practical choices for a Gloucester seller?
sections.html:
Sellers in Gloucester tend to face an older house, a coastal exposure issue, or a property that is hard to maintain from a distance. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can take on those conditions. A traditional listing may bring more attention in summer and slow down in winter.

Before you decide, get the transfer inspection scheduled, confirm the tax installment status, and decide whether the buyer will take over any rental permit. Those three items are the ones most likely to hold up a closing.

faqs.q: Is Gloucester a city or a town?
faqs.a: Gloucester is a city. It was settled in 1623, incorporated as a town in 1642 and reincorporated as a city in 1873, with a mayor and council form of government.

faqs.q: When are Gloucester property tax bills issued?
faqs.a: Bills are scheduled to be issued July 1, October 1, January 1 and April 1, and each is due 30 days after it is issued.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to apply for a property tax abatement in Gloucester?
faqs.a: The window runs from the third quarter bill, typically January 1, to its due date, typically February 1. The deadline is firm and the Assessors cannot grant an abatement after it.

faqs.q: Does Gloucester require an inspection when a house is sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The Fire Prevention Bureau handles real estate transfer inspections, scheduled through the city's online permitting system, and the building must display a house number.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Gloucester house short term?
faqs.a: Only with a short-term rental permit. The city's ordinance has applied since April 1, 2025, and covers rentals of 30 days or less.
